Disclosure  to  Promote  the  Right  To  Information 

Whereas  the  Parliament  of  India  has  set  out  to  provide  a  practical  regime  of  right  to 
information  for  citizens  to  secure  access  to  information  under  the  control  of  public  authorities, 
in  order  to  promote  transparency  and  accountability  in  the  working  of  every  public  authority, 
and  whereas  the  attached  publication  of  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards  is  of  particular  interest 
to  the  public,  particularly  disadvantaged  communities  and  those  engaged  in  the  pursuit  of 
education  and  knowledge,  the  attached  public  safety  standard  is  made  available  to  promote  the 
timely  dissemination  of  this  information  in  an  accurate  manner  to  the  public. 


Mazdoor  Kisan  Shakti  Sangathan 
"The  Right  to  Information,  The  Right  to  Live"

Indian  Standard 

SPECIFICATION  FOR 
BENDING    BARS 


IS:  7077-  1973 


(  Reaffirmed  2006 )

1.  Scope  —  Lays  down  the  general  requirements  for  bending  bars. 

2.  Dimensions 


All  dimensions  in  millimetres. 
2.1   Normal  engineering  tolerances  shall  apply  to  the  untoleranced  dimensions. 

3.  Material  —  Suitable  steels  shall  be  used  for  the  manufacture  of  bending  bars. 

Example  : 

C20  and  C25  of  Schedule  ii  of  iS  :  1  570-1  961  s  Schedules  for  wrought  steels  for  general 
engineering  purposes'  with  a  maximum  sulphur  and  phosphorus  content  of  0*05  percent 
each. 

4.  Manufacture  —  The  bending  bars  shall  be  soundly  forged  to  shape  as  shown  in  the  figure  and  shall 
be  free  from  pits,  rust,  cracks  and  other  defects  and  shall  be  finished  smooth  all  over. 

5.  Preservation  and  Packing  —  The  bending  bars  shaM  be  given  proper  rust-preventive  treatment 
before  packing  and  shall  be  packed  in  accordance  with  the  best  prevalent  trade  practice. 

6.  Sampling  —  Unless  otherwise  agreed  to  between  the  supplier  and  the  purchaser,  the  procedure 
given  in  IS  :  2500  (  Part  I  )-1963  '  Inspection  by  attributes  and  by  count  of  defects  :  Part  I  '  shall  be 
followed  for  sampling  inspection.  The  sampling  plan  for  various  characteristics  shall  be  as  given 
in  6.1. 

6.1  For  examining  dimensions  and  other  requirements  sampling  plans  with  inspection  level  til  and 
acceptable  quality  level  (  AQt  )  2*5  percent  given  in  Tables  1  and  2  of  IS  :  2500  (  Part  I  )-1963  shall 
be  followed. 

7.  Marking  —  The  bending  bars  shall  be  marked  with  manufacturer's  name,  initials  or  recognized  trade- 
mark. 

7.1    Certification  Marking  —  Details    available    with    the    Bureau  of  Indian  Standards. 


EXPLANATORY     NOTE 

This  standard  deals  with  bending  bars  (also  known  as  bending  bolts)  chiefly  employed  by 
plumbers  for  bending  pipes.  While  preparing  this  standard,  assistance  has  been  derived  from  Drawing 
No.  CIGS/Tools/71  '  Bolts,  bending  '  issued  by  the  Chief  Inspectorate  of  General  Stores,  Kanpur. 


Adopted  26  November  1973 


<g)  December  1973,  BIS 


Gr  1
